system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller’s “FINAL”, principal-agreement and market-standard assertions are not evidence of Buyer agreement. The recommendations below assume the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free acquisition baseline; underlying DD documents and the complete SPA still require review.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery supported by Seller creditworthiness; separate protection for excluded categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, with any reduction conditional on the overall protection package and recovery security—20% may leave significant acquisition losses uninsured. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible** basket, recovering only excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, aggregation of related claims, and exclusions for specially protected claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related claims—Seller’s combination materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate category periods, and preservation of timely notified contingent claims. | **Counter at 24 months and reject blanket application**—Buyer needs sufficient reporting cycles to identify breaches. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties, no thresholds, price-level recovery and a substantially longer claim period. | **Require a 100% price cap and seven-year contractual notification period**, subject to applicable law—ownership and authority are core acquisition risks, not ordinary warranty risks. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is identified. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent-misrepresentation claims, remedies and reliance, including appropriate attribution to Seller. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**—Seller must not obtain contractual protection for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, against identified warranties, in a frozen record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific, fairly detailed disclosures and an archived index**—document availability is not adequate identification of a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters merely discoverable from records. | No knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel of the relevant breach. | **Delete; alternatively exclude constructive, imputed and adviser knowledge and any duty to investigate**—Seller’s wording transfers undiscovered diligence risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied by delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or satisfaction evidence. | Completion conditional on effective consent and satisfaction of all applicable conditions, without materially adverse amendments. | **Require evidence addressing clauses 11.2–11.3, with waiver solely for Buyer**—a conditional consent letter alone may not protect approximately 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Full payoff and effective release at Completion, with debt deducted through the agreed price mechanics. | **Require a lender payoff letter and binding simultaneous discharge arrangements, paying the lender directly**—Buyer should not acquire an encumbered business or fund Seller debt twice. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses called a Seller matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unresolved. | Seller-funded treatment of transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable on-costs, including liabilities payable after Completion. | **Itemise and deduct or reserve the liability, verify conditions/on-costs and obtain a specific indemnity without double recovery**—omission otherwise shifts transaction costs to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; transfer depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; AUD 180,000 recorded open. | Verified payment and complete chain of title, backed by protection for ownership defects and resulting losses. | **Require cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment by Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice amount**—payment exposure and missing IP ownership are different risks. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, expected immaterial; access, scope and notification requirements remain unconfirmed. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal assessment and protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation/remediation covenants and a separate indemnity, with a Completion condition if findings establish material risk**—uncertainty does not establish either a confirmed breach or immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assessment together of timing, scope, commitment, termination rights and accounting treatment. | **Review the AUD 330,000 aggregate commitment and allocate through price adjustment or consent controls where justified**—neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment follows from the disclosed amounts alone. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims. | Expressly differentiated treatment of general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, payment/adjustment obligations, covenants and fraud. | **Rewrite definitions and cross-references with an express precedence clause**—a global limitation can silently defeat negotiated category-specific protection. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller owns 100%. | Independent confirmation of issued capital, legal/beneficial ownership, encumbrances, options and competing rights, plus effective transfer documents. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, certificates and capital history; obtain searches, releases and title warranties**—the register is evidence, not complete verification of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tailored tax periods; robust IP warranties and specific protection for identified defects. | **Keep both open: negotiate tax protection aligned with assessment periods/extensions and a longer, appropriately capped IP regime**—general limits inadequately address historic tax exposure and ownership of the core technology. |

**Priority:** secure Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay title and bonus funding before Completion; resolve the incident investigation and preserve separate liability regimes in parallel.
=== END ADVICE ===
